findings.claim: The rationale's first foreclosure of distractor C over-reads the passage: it upgrades a sentence scoped to one group of farmers into a universal claim that the Sunday crying was the only channel of notice for every owner.
findings.evidence: Rationale: "it forecloses the reading twice - notice ran through the Sunday crying and no other channel, and both beasts were in fact fetched on the same Sunday." The passage supports only a scoped version: "Skellorne was to cry what he held at the church door each Sunday after service, and nowhere else." (a restriction on where/when HE cried) and "Farmers on the far side of the common heard of a beast no other way." (explicitly limited to far-side farmers; the qualifier "on the far side" implies nearer owners could learn some other way, e.g. by seeing the pound, which the passage places "behind the church"). The same over-read recurs in generator_meta.key_derivation ("the once-a-week crying that was the only notice") and engineered_traps ("foreclosed by the Sunday-only notice").
findings.why: Does not change the SOUND verdict. The rationale's primary refutation of C is airtight and textually exact ("the passage says nothing about when either owner missed his beast"), and the second foreclosure quotes verbatim and independently defeats C ("Both were fetched on the Sunday they were cried"). Key B is likewise unaffected: both 1851 cases were in fact redeemed on the crying Sunday, so the paired bills still support B. But the rationale is the student-facing teaching payload, so an over-statement of what the passage says is worth tightening to the scoped form.

findings.claim: generator_meta.spelling_note offers as BrE spelling evidence a list of words that contain no BrE-vs-AmE orthographic discriminator; the unit's BrE identity is lexical/period, not orthographic.
findings.evidence: spelling_note: "BrE held throughout passage, prompt and options: 'pinder', 'vestry', 'smithy', 'shilling', 'sixpence', 'heifer', 'reckoning', 'roofless'." Of these, 'heifer', 'reckoning' and 'roofless' are spelled identically in AmE and are not variety markers at all; 'pinder', 'vestry', 'smithy', 'shilling', 'sixpence' are lexical/period items, not spellings. The passage contains no -ise/-ize, -our/-or, -re/-er, -ll-/-l- or -ae-/-e- discriminator anywhere.
findings.why: Does not change the CLEAR verdict. The operative requirement is met on the student-facing text: no AmE spelling and no AmE-only idiom appears, and the BrE constructions that do discriminate are correct ('taken up on a Monday', 'on the Saturday of that same week', 'one and sixpence', 'between times', 'at its owner's charge'). The defect is in the meta's stated evidence, not in the English.
